chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Mu'ammār ibn Khallād from Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'What do people narrate from you regarding clay and their dislike of it?' He said, 'That is the wet clay, and that is the dry clay.'

key_terms.الطِّين: Clay, specifically referring to the earth used for prostration
key_terms.كَرَاهِيَتِهِ: His dislike (referring to a specific ruling or preference)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between wet and dry clay regarding prostration in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) clarifies the distinction between two types of clay used for prostration, resolving the apparent contradiction in narrations by specifying that the 'dislike' applies only to wet clay (al-mablūl), whereas dry clay (al-madar) is permissible. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the physical state of the material—specifically its moisture content—affects its ritual purity and suitability for sajah. The ruling underscores the importance of precise material conditions in acts of worship, ensuring that the prostration is performed on a clean and stable surface.
